svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 3. Four questions before installing, and the stacks they produce
svg.desc: On the left, four questions to ask before installing any extension: whether a browser setting already does it, whether you can name the current maintainer, whether the permissions match the job, and whether you will notice if it changes hands. On the right, the resulting minimal stacks for Firefox, Brave, Chrome and Tor Browser.
svg.text: Figure 3: Four Questions, and What Survives Them
Question 1 removes most candidates on its own. Very few extensions survive all four.
Does a browser setting already do this?

g.text: A setting costs no entropy, needs no trust, and cannot be sold to
anybody. It wins every time it is an option.
Retired by this question: forced encryption, canvas control, storage isolation.

svg.text: Can you name who maintains it now?

g.text: Not who wrote it. Who ships the updates today. Ownership changes
are how good extensions become bad ones, quietly, after install.
If the answer is a company you have never heard of, stop here.

svg.text: Do the permissions match the job?

g.text: A content blocker genuinely needs to read every page. A currency
converter does not. Compare what it asks for against what it does.
A mismatch here is the clearest signal you will ever get.

svg.text: Will you notice if it changes?

g.text: Extensions update themselves silently. If you will not review this
one again, you are trusting it permanently and in advance.
Put a date in the calendar, or do not install it.

svg.text: Four yes answers, or it does not go on.

g.text: The full content blocker, which still has its complete
capability here. Containers for separation.
Two. Possibly a third for cleaning addresses.
Its blocking already runs below the extension layer, so
most of what you would add is duplication.
Zero, in most cases. Add nothing by default.
Only the reduced blocker is available. No extension
choice recovers what the platform removed.
One, and understand that it does less.
Adding anything moves you out of the group of identical
users that is the entire protection.
None. Not one. This is not a recommendation, it is the design.
